item.description: Criciúma take Série B playoff lead; Atlético-GO and Vila Nova draw Criciúma beat Fortaleza 1-0 in the first leg of the Série B promotion playoffs Credits: Celso da Luz/ Criciúma E.C. Press Office Criciúma moved closer to securing promotion to Série A with a 1-0 win over Fortaleza on Sunday (22). The result at Heriberto Hulse, secured by a goal from Marcelo Hermes, means a draw will be enough for the Santa Catarina side in the second leg of the Série B playoffs. That match will take place on Saturday (28), at 8 p.m. (Brasília time), at Arena Castelão in Fortaleza. Leão do Pici need a win by any margin to secure promotion. This is because, if the aggregate score is level, the promotion spot will go to the team that finished higher in the league. In this case, that is Fortaleza, who finished fourth, while Criciúma finished fifth. In the other matchup, Atlético-GO and Vila Nova drew 1-1 at Antônio Accioly in Goiânia. item.title: TSU fires Cris Dishman, a former Houston Oilers star, after three years at helm of football program
item.description: Cris Dishman spent three seasons as head coach at Texas Southern, going 14-19. (Jeff Curry/Getty Images) Two days after getting routed in the season finale by Arkansas-Pine Bluff , Texas Southern University announced the dismissal of head coach Cris Dishman on Monday morning. After going 11-11 in his first two seasons at the helm, the former Houston Oilers defensive back went 3-8 with the Tigers this year, including a last-place finish in the SWAC at 2-6. "I want to thank Coach Dishman for his hard work and dedication to Texas Southern University and our football program," TSU athletic director Ashley Robinson said in a statement released by the school. "We wish Coach Dishman well moving forward." Robinson took over at TSU three months ago after leaving the athletic director's post at Jackson State, where he had previously hired Deion Sanders. When Dishman, who replaced Clarence McKinney, was hired in 2024 , he took over a program that had gone though 13 straight losing seasons. He went 5-6 in Year 1, but snapped the Tigers' nine-game losing streak to rival Prairie View A&M in his head coaching debut. The Tigers finally got over the hump in 2025, going 6-5 for their first winning season since 2010. After beating North Carolina Central in this year's season opener, Dishman's third year took a turn with a 52-14 loss to Prairie View A&M in a game that was nationally televised by ESPN. The Tigers won just two of their final nine games, including getting beat 42-17 by Arkansas-Pine Bluff on Saturday. Dishman, 61, played 13 seasons in the NFL, including his first nine with the Oilers (1988-96) where he was a first-team All-Pro selection in 1991. When Dishman was hired in 2024, he was coming off a stint as the defensive coordinator for the XFL's Las Vegas Vipers. He also had previously spent time as an NFL assistant with the Raiders (2005, 2007), Dolphins (2006), Chargers (2009-12) and Cardinals (2017). He also was Baylor's safeties coaching from 2015-16. item.title: Brewers Should Sign Free Agent Pitcher They Traded To Royals Last Offseason
item.description: Free agent pitcher Nick Mears The Kansas City Royals designated Nick Mears for assignment on Nov. 17, and he is now a free agent. The Milwaukee Brewers traded Mears to the Royals last offseason, and a reunion could make sense. The Brewers already lost Dustin May, who was a part of their bullpen in October. They could lose JoJo Romero as well. Bringing back Mears could be a cheap but solid move. Mears had a 3.49 ERA with the Brewers in 2025 and appeared in 63 games for the team. He played a huge role in the Brewers winning the most games in baseball in 2025 and reaching the National League Championship Series. Mears was originally acquired by the Brewers in 2024, but did not really find his footing until the postseason. It was similar to what happened with Romero this year. The Brewers worked with him, and his chase rate was in the 93rd percentile in 2025. In five postseason games with the Brewers between 2024 and 2025, he worked four innings and did not allow any runs. Last season, Mears only pitched in 21 big league games. He dealt with a shoulder injury and a lat injury before ultimately undergoing surgery for thoracic outlet syndrome. He had a 5.12 ERA last season, and he could be open to returning to a team he had success on. The Brewers have a reputation for fixing broken pitchers, and taking a flyer on Mears would be a low-risk move. If he can return to the form he was in during the 2025 season, he would be a great addition to the bullpen.

item.description: Nathan Ray Seebeck-Imagn Images Capitals reward recent waiver pickup with 2-year contract extension appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Jack St. Ivany has made an impact in his first month with the Washington Capitals , chipping in a goal and seven points in 11 games. The defenseman — who was claimed from the Winnipeg Jets on Oct. 24 — was rewarded for his strong play Monday, signing a two-year, $2.35 million contract extension , general manager Chris Patrick announced. The deal carries an average annual value of $1.175 million. Since making his Capitals debut at the end of October, the 27-year-old is tied for second among the team’s defensemen in assists (six) and ranks third in points (seven) and fifth in hits (10), per the official release. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Averaging a shade over 14 minutes per game between Washington and Winnipeg, St. Ivany was the first player in franchise history to record multiple assists in each of his first two games with the Caps. He scored his first career goal in a 4-3 victory over the Florida Panthers on Nov. 7. The Manhattan Beach, California native was originally selected in the fourth round, No. 112 overall, by the Philadelphia Flyers in the 2018 NHL Draft. The 6-foot-4 blueliner played collegiately at Yale University and Boston College, amassing 60 points in 115 games. He also won a silver medal with the United States at the 2019 IIHF World Junior Championship. Left unsigned after college, St. Ivany broke into the NHL with the Pittsburgh Penguins after spending a couple of years with AHL affiliate Wilkes-Barre/Scranton, appearing in 14 games in 2023-24 and 19 contests in 2024-25. He split last season between the minors and the NHL, posting seven assists in 20 regular-season games with the Penguins. He was traded to the Jets in exchange for David Gustafsson in June 2026 and made Winnipeg’s opening-night roster out of training camp. St. Ivany made four appearances on the blue line in a third-pairing role before being placed on waivers and subsequently claimed by the Capitals. The right-shot defenseman seems to have found his stride in the nation’s capital, and the extension gives him an opportunity to establish himself as an NHL regular. He’s currently playing on the third pairing ahead of extra defenseman Timothy Liljegren. It remains to be seen what role he will play when Rasmus Sandin is ready to return from a torn ACL the Swede sustained in April. Losers of five straight, the Capitals are back in action against the Philadelphia Flyers on Wednesday night. item.title: Texas S Kobe Black out for season
item.description: AUSTIN, TEXAS - NOVEMBER 28: Kobe Black #6 of the Texas Longhorns celerbates a interception during the fourth quarter of a game against the Texas A&M Aggies at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium on November 28, 2025 in Austin, Texas. (Photo by Alex Slitz/Getty Images) | Getty Images AUSTIN — During his Monday press conference, Texas Longhorns head coach Steve Sarkisian confirmed a report from On Texas Football that junior safety Kobe Black will miss the remainder of the season after suffering an injury during Saturday’s win over the Arkansas Razorbacks. “I hate it for him. It’s disappointing,” Sarkisian said. “He was having a really good year for us with the position change.” Late in the first half, Black went down grabbing his left knee after attempting to make a tackle on a short completion by Arkansas quarterback KJ Jackson. Black spent a significant amount of time down on the field before he was helped into the locker room by trainers. After switching from cornerback to safety during the offseason, Black earned the starting free safety role over senior Derek Williams in the season opener against Texas State, but dealt with injuries throughout the season, missing the UTSA and Ole Miss games, but ultimately starting five times. Black’s season ends with 21 tackles (nine solo) and one pass broken up, steadying a Texas career that was on the brink of ending in disappointment after the Waco Connally product entered the NCAA transfer portal before withdrawing his name and returning to the Forty Acres after the Longhorns made a “strong push” to keep him in the program. As a member of the 2024 recruiting class, Black was a major late addition for Texas as a consensus five-star prospect ranked as the No. 34 player nationally and the No. 5 cornerback in the 247Sports Composite rankings. Black is the fourth major contributor for the Longhorns who is ruled out of the season after Sarkisian left open the possibility that fifth-year defensive tackle Hero Kanu could return in the playoffs after undergoing bicep surgery.

item.title: United States announced as 2031 Women’s World Cup co-host
item.description: ZURICH — The United States is going to be a soccer World Cup host again in 2031 and England will do so for the first time since 1966. FIFA on Monday confirmed the U.S. will lead a four-nation, regional co-hosting of the 2031 Women’s World Cup — with Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica — and a UK project led by England was ratified for the 2035 edition. The winning candidates and FIFA president Gianni Infantino promised commercially successful tournaments — the first editions with 48 teams and 104 games — and to reinvest all that money in women’s soccer. “This will be the largest women’s sporting event in history,” the U.S. Soccer Federation president, Cindy Parlow Cone, told FIFA members in a pre-vote presentation at the governing body’s headquarters in Zurich. “Which means we have to deliver.” Rose Lavelle of the United States plays during an international friendly soccer match against Japan in San Jose, Calif., Saturday, April 11, 2026. AP FIFA wanted these heavyweights of women’s soccer to face no opposition without rival bids and so lead hosting the first expanded tournaments . That will bring parity with the men’s World Cup which expanded to 48 teams this year in the U.S., Canada and Mexico. The 2027 Women’s World Cup will have 32 teams in Brazil. The U.S.-led 2031 project across the CONCACAF regional soccer body bid offers FIFA a choice of stadiums in 20 cities: 14 in the U.S., four in Mexico plus San José in Costa Rica and Kingston, Jamaica. Spain’s Alexia Putellas, left, Jennifer Hermoso and Irene Paredes celebrate winning the Women’s World Cup final in Sydney, Australia, Aug. 20, 2023. AP The United Kingdom bid joins England with Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales that offers a choice from 19 venues, including Wembley Stadium in London. The pair of four-nation co-hosting bids had a clear run in the past 20 months and were approved Monday by acclamation in an online meeting of FIFA’s 211 member federations. The U.S. previously hosted the Women’s World Cup alone in 1999 and 2003. The national team’s tournament win in 1999 was the second of its four titles. England never hosted a Women’s World Cup which started with the 1991 tournament in China, won by the U.S. In the men’s World Cup, England hosted for the only time in 1966 and won its only title.

item.title: Nick Bosa’s postgame gesture to Mexico City 49ers fans speaks volumes
item.description: San Francisco 49ers star edge rusher Nick Bosa was awash in boos from Mexico City fans when being introduced Sunday. This appeared to be the byproduct of Bosa’s comments from earlier in the week, when he made a request about how fans at the game should cheer . “I think we need some, like, information given to the fans so they know when to cheer. ’Cause, uh, they just chant the whole time,” Bosa said Wednesday. Nick Bosa (No. 97) of the San Francisco 49ers said he wants “information given to the fans so they know when to cheer.” Getty Images “But yeah, if we could kind of teach them — no offense to them and their soccer cheering techniques — but if they could cheer when we’re on defense, that would be great,” he added. View this post on Instagram The comments likely irked some fans who plausibly felt Bosa’s comments implied fans in Mexico didn’t know the rules of American football or when the correct time to cheer was. However, some others didn’t seem to mind what Bosa said — and there were certainly many who showered him with love in Mexico City, as seen in a video from Instagram user @49ers.cam, showing Bosa approaching the stands after beating the Vikings and throwing his gloves into the crowd. Bosa engaging with Niners fans in Mexico City after beating the Minnesota Vikings. The star edge rusher throwing his gloves into the crowd after the 49ers beat the Minnesota Vikings in Mexico City. Fans were cheering him on throughout the exchange, as the camera then followed Bosa as he walked into the locker room, high-fiving young fans. item.title: 'There was a time in my career when I was playing all three format': KL Rahul
item.description: NEW DELHI: KL Rahul has opened up about the challenges he faced while trying to balance Test cricket with the demands of ODIs and T20Is. The Indian batter admitted that switching between formats was not easy earlier in his career, as each required a different approach, mindset and preparation. Rahul recently made history with his 136-run knock against New Zealand at the Basin Reserve. He became the first Indian opener to score Test centuries in all four SENA countries (South Africa, England, New Zealand and Australia). He is also only the second Asian opener after Saeed Anwar to achieve the feat. His century was the first by an Indian batter in New Zealand in 12 years. Speaking in a video shared on bcci.tv, Rahul explained how experience and missed opportunities helped him understand the demands of Test cricket. "There was a time in my career when I was playing all three format... I could not make that switch from trying to get bat on ball in T20 and ODI cricket to switching quickly in a week's time to leaving balls and trying to play as late as I possibly can, which is the basics of Test batting," said Rahul. Rahul on preparation and the demands of Test cricket The 34-year-old said Test cricket requires patience, careful preparation and a different way of thinking compared to limited-overs formats. He compared his batting approach to his passion for making coffee, explaining how even a small mistake can affect the final result. "Patience and the preparation, you get one tiny thing wrong and the (coffee) cup is going to taste bad. I think it's the same in Test cricket... one small mistake, one bad shot as a batter and your whole innings can mean nothing even if you've worked hard for three or four hours," he said. Rahul also revealed that he starts preparing mentally five or six months before challenging overseas tours, studying conditions and planning how to tackle them. Rahul opens up about injuries and missed opportunities Despite his historic century, Rahul said the achievement left him emotional and unable to sleep. "Honestly, I've not slept at all the whole night and it's not because of excitement," he said. The batter also expressed disappointment over injuries that have interrupted his career, believing they may have cost him at least 10-15 Test appearances. Having played 71 Tests, Rahul hopes to remain fit, continue scoring runs and finish the final phase of his career strongly.

item.title: 'Not So Happy Valley!': Chris Carlin erupts as Rutgers stuns Penn State
item.description: Credit: @ChrisCarlin on X / Matthew O'Haren-Imagn Images Rutgers had to wait 38 years to beat Penn State again, and Chris Carlin made sure the radio audience heard every one of those years in his voice when it finally happened. The Scarlet Knights stunned the Nittany Lions 25-24 on Saturday before more than 106,000 people at Beaver Stadium, snapping an 18-game losing streak in the series and earning their first victory in State College since 1988. Greg Schiano’s group arrived in Happy Valley at 2-8, an underdog by nearly four touchdowns, and trailed 24-10 heading into the fourth quarter before ripping off 15 unanswered points over the final 10 minutes. The decisive touchdown came out of a finish so improbable it felt borrowed from a backyard game. On the final play of regulation, AJ Surace found Antwan Raymond near the goal line, and with a pair of Penn State defensive backs wrapped around his waist, Raymond flipped the ball to Ben Black III, who strolled the last three yards into the end zone. And in the chaos of the pileup, Carlin and everyone listening on the Rutgers radio network had no idea Black had scored. They found out only when the referee announced the touchdown over the stadium microphone, which drew a stunned “WHAT?!” from Carlin. As requested, Chris Carlin’s call of the touchdown. I had the same exact reaction as Chris when I heard the ref say it was a touchdown over the stadium mic: “WHAT?!” https://t.co/ZbbomROolL — Brian Fonseca (@briannnnf) November 22, 2026 Rather than send out his kicker to tie the game and take his chances in overtime against a team favored by nearly four touchdowns, Schiano kept his offense on the field and put the season, and 38 years of frustration, on a single snap from the 3-yard line. Carlin has been the radio voice of Rutgers football since 2004, which means he has narrated an entire generation of losses to Penn State. Since Rutgers joined the Big Ten in 2014, the Scarlet Knights have lost all 12 conference meetings with the Nittany Lions. item.title: Discussion: How many more wins do the Panthers need to win the division?
item.description: CHARLOTTE, NC - NOVEMBER 08: Carolina Panthers helmet during an NFL football game between the Denver Broncos and the Carolina Panthers on November 8, 2026, at Bank of America Stadium in Charlotte, N.C. (Photo by John Byrum/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Carolina Panthers squeaked out a 35-33 win over the Baltimore Ravens on Sunday in a game that featured all sorts of twists and turns. The win gets them back to .500. They now have a commanding two game lead over the rest of the NFC South, where every other team is 3-7. The Panthers have seven games left, one against each of the rest of the NFC South, and four against non-divisional opponents. The four other games are significantly harder. They play at the Vikings, home against the Bengals, at the Steelers, and home against the Seahawks. The only one of those four teams that’s not currently in the playoffs is the Seahawks, and they’re the defending Super Bowl champions and have a 6-4 record. It’s going to be hard for the Panthers to find wins there. Meanwhile, the Saints and Buccaneers have much easier paths as they try to catch up to Carolina. The Saints have a game with the Cardinals and a couple of chances to make up ground against the Buccaneers. Those very Buccaneers only have one game left against a team with a winning record—the Rams in Week 17. So that brings us to our question: How many more games do the Panthers need to win to win the division? MY TAKE: 4. Four wins would feel like almost a sure bet to make the playoffs. Someone would have to win out to overtake Carolina straight up and would have to go 6-1 the rest of the way just to tie. Three games might be enough, particularly if one of them is against Tampa Bay on Monday night. If the Panthers lose that, there’s going to be a lot of pressure to create some distance over Tampa given their easier schedule and the tiebreaker advantage they’d have. The easiest way for that to happen is for the Panthers to sweep the three games against their relatively weak divisional foes. Then they’d have to steal just one game from outside of the division, and the best chance for that to happen would be Week 16 against the Steelers.

item.description: FORT MYERS, FLORIDA - MARCH 7: Johan Oviedo #29 of the Boston Red Sox looks on in the dugout before a spring training game against the Tampa Bay Rays at JetBlue Park at Fenway South on March 7, 2026 in Fort Myers, Florida. (Photo by Maddie Malhotra/Boston Red Sox/Getty Images) | Getty Images On Nov. 20 the Diamondbacks acquired right-hander Johan Oviedo from the Red Sox for minor-league lefty Luke Dotson and a player to be named later or cash. It’s an easy trade to scroll past: a 28-year-old starter who struggles to throw strikes and has thrown 44 big-league innings since 2023, coming off Tommy John surgery, a lat strain and an elbow strain. But a year ago this exact pitcher cost Boston its No. 6 prospect. The reason is likely tied strongly to one pitch, and it’s still there. The Fastball That Changed In 2023, Oviedo’s four-seamer was hard and flat. It averaged 95.8 mph with 10.2 inches of induced vertical break (IVB), well below average for a four-seamer that firm. Despite the velocity and the elite extension from Oviedo’s massive body at 6’6”, hitters didn’t miss it: an 18% whiff rate per swing, and a Stuff+ of 91, 34th percentile among MLB four-seamers. The breaking balls weren’t the problem. In 2023 his slider (+11.2 runs) and curveball (+4.6) saved about 16 runs combined, while the four-seamer cost him 6.4. Per pitch, the slider and curve were above average (62nd and 70th percentile in run value per 100), and much of the +16 comes from volume: together they were half his pitches. This put Oviedo in the 98th percentile in baseball on statcast’s breaking run value. Despite having a well below average fastball by stuff+ in just the 34th percentile, Oviedo was able to rely on his breaking pitches to pitch to a respectable 4.31 ERA. He would then miss all of 2024 after Tommy John surgery. When he came back in August 2025, the fastball was very different: His IVB jumps off the page. Five extra inches of ride at the same velocity is a big change. What’s interesting is how he got it. The usual way to add ride is to raise the arm slot and get more over the top. Oviedo went the other way: his arm angle dropped from about 28° to 24° and his release point fell about 2.6 inches. The ride came from the spin itself. Less of his movement went sideways (run fell by almost 4 inches) and more went straight up. That’s the sign of truer backspin. The combination is what hitters hate. A lower release plus more carry means the ball arrives on a flatter plane (-4.16° vs -5.05°), so it stays above barrels at the top of the zone. Add elite extension and the 95.5 mph plays like about 97. How Rare is a Gain Like This? item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. But he wasn’t the right fit for the Crew in the post-Nancy era. The Crew turned to Courtois, a former Crew academy and MLS Next Pro coach who continued the idea first expressed on the field so successfully by Nancy’s teams. item.description: They came by car, by the special-event X80 bus, by bike if they were feeling sporty. They came in layers, in beanies and scarves, with Gotham’s black-and-sky-blue colors on top. They came on behalf of those who couldn’t come, capacity being reduced at this impromptu change of venue, each one trying to make noise for five. And then, 25 miles and 20,000 seats removed from their regular destination at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium, huddled in the bleachers by a blue track ringing an immaculate pitch at Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island, in the shadow of the old Psychiatric Center and with the light fading over the Costco across the river, 5,000 devoted souls Sunday afternoon watched Gotham’s NWSL title defense end in a 2-1 semifinal loss to the Kansas City Current. “We lost today because we weren’t the better team,” Gotham winger and oracle Midge Purce said. “That being said, I would say it’s inexcusable. It’s not what you want in a professional league. It’s not what you want for women who are progressing in the United States and supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it’s a bad look for everyone involved. And we always want to be at Sports Illustrated in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. item.title: On MLS Decision Day, D.C. United faces a familiar reality: Another season of failure
item.description: WASHINGTON — All around Major League Soccer , from Montreal to Miami and Seattle to San Diego, Saturday was Decision Day — the last act in an 8½-month production. While three playoff berths were in the balance, teams with guaranteed spots sought to improve their place. It's a day marked by desperation, scoreboard-watching and playoff-planning. At Audi Field, however, Decision Day felt more like Derision Day. For the seventh consecutive year, D.C. United, once a showpiece of a blossoming league, has no playoff plans — a near impossibility in a league that distributes postseason passes like a guy on a New York street corner handing out flyers for discount mattresses. Only Toronto FC's eight-year rut, starting with its 2007 expansion campaign, lasted longer. United wasn't even in the mix on Decision Day, its fate having been decided 10 days earlier. The lowly finale was against another failed side, New York City FC, which claimed a 1-0 victory on a late goal. While 2026 was an anomaly for the New Yorkers, it was the norm in the nation's capital. D.C. added another sad chapter to a rotten story under an ownership group, led by Jason Levien and Steve Kaplan, that has dragged the organization into irrelevance in not just the prospering league but in the local market and the ascending sport. The public-address announcer introduces the team as "your four-time MLS Cup champions," but he's been saying that for a long time. Given the league's evolution, it feels even longer. United's last title, in 2004, came in a 10-team operation — one-third the current landscape. Since then, 13 different clubs have hoisted the trophy. Less than two miles north of Audi Field, the U.S. Capitol witnessed a historic sea change Tuesday with a political wave that swept the ruling party out of office. Local soccer fans have had no such luck with those in power at Audi Field. Under the current regime … United hasn't won a playoff game in 11 years and hasn't advanced to the conference finals in 14. Twelve years have passed since it won at least half its 34 matches. United's only trophy in recent memory was the 2013 U.S. Open Cup, which came amid a horrific, three-win regular season. D.C. is on its fourth head coach since Ben Olsen's departure in late 2020 and its second head of soccer operations in four years. The current director, Erkut Sogut — an agent best known for representing former German star Mesut Özil — was hired last fall without any experience working for a team. Another goal conceded, another season to forget. Keisuke Kurokawa's frustration summed up D.C. United's latest disappointing chapter. Scott Taetsch via Getty Images United remains one of three MLS organizations without a developmental team bridging the youth academy to the first team.
